# W1 handoff: Platform (Blob store, Jobs, GC)

Workstream W1 of [`15-build-plan.md`](../../spec/15-build-plan.md), on branch `ws/w1-platform` from the phase 0 commit `b3ed701`. Changes outside W1's paths are in [`requests/w1.md`](../requests/w1.md).

## Done, by feature ID

| Feature | What | Where |
|---|---|---|
| OPS-1 | Filesystem Blob store: objects at `<root>/<key>`, writes staged under `<root>/.staging` and renamed into place (retrying when a concurrent Delete prunes the destination directory), multipart parts under `uploads/<id>/`, no file locks (works on NFS and SMB). `SweepStaging` removes staging files a crash or a killed process left behind. | `internal/blob/fs` |
| OPS-1 | S3-compatible Blob store on minio-go: static or chain credentials (environment, shared file, IAM, IRSA), path-style option, key prefix, multipart, presigned GET, PUT and part URLs, server-side copy over 5 GiB with `ComposeObject`. | `internal/blob/s3` |
| OPS-1 | Opening the configured backend, with a bucket check at start-up. | `internal/blob/backends` |
| OPS-1 | Spans per Blob store operation and `hangar.blob.operation.duration`, recording key prefixes but never full keys or presigned URLs. A failed operation records an `exception` event with the innermost error's Go type and a fixed description (a sentinel's text, an S3 error code through `blob.CodedError`, an operating system error such as `file exists`, or a network timeout or error), never the error's text, which holds full keys and, on the filesystem, the root path. The errors themselves keep their detail for callers; the filesystem backend's install errors name the key, not absolute paths. | `blob.Instrument`, `internal/blob/fs`, `internal/blob/s3` |
| UP-5 | Streaming writes up to 5 TiB: `blob.PutVerified` (visible only if the SHA-256 matches), `blob.PutMultipart`, `blob.PartSize` (max(16 MiB, ceil(size/10000))). S3 streams parts with no part buffer; unknown-size S3 Puts buffer one part (16 MiB, doubling every 2,000 parts to 128 MiB, so over 700 GiB). | `internal/blob/verified.go`, `internal/blob/s3` |
| DOWN-2 | Download policy: a presigned redirect on S3 in `redirect` mode, streaming otherwise (`Downloads.Serve`, with Range, HEAD and 416), with `expires_in` for LFS batch responses. Every download is `application/octet-stream` with an attachment `Content-Disposition`; streamed ones also send `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`. Presigned PUTs can sign `x-amz-checksum-sha256` and then sign the pinned `Content-Type` too. | `blob.Downloads`, `blob.SetDownloadHeaders`, `backends.Downloads`, `docs/research/s3-presigned-checksum.md` |
| Jobs (02) | Database Job queue on SQLite and Postgres: dedupe on (kind, key) while pending or running, priorities, `RunAfter`, cascading cancel of child Jobs, retry, cursor listing, trace context stored at enqueue, `EnqueueTx` for enqueuing in a caller's transaction, `NewJob.Repo` for Repo-scoped Jobs (kept on retry). | `jobs.DBQueue` |
| Jobs (02) | Worker: claims with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` (Postgres) or a write transaction (SQLite), lease renewal at a third of the lease, progress and result writes fenced on the lease owner and the attempt number (a run whose Job was requeued and claimed again, even by the same worker, stops at its next write and its result is discarded), retry with backoff, `Permanent` errors, timeouts, panic recovery, lease-expiry recovery, cancel of running handlers, release without using an attempt on shutdown, handler errors redacted (`jobs.RedactError`: no URL query strings or user information) before they reach spans, logs or the Job's error column, panics stored as a fixed message with the stack logged server-side only, `jobs.Snooze` (for pull windows), Instance-wide limits per kind (for `pull.file` at `pull.concurrency`), per-process limits per kind (`HandlerOptions.Concurrency`, which `gc` and `upload.expire` set to 1; a claim never takes more than the room left, and the tighter limit wins when a kind has both), spans linked to the enqueuing span, `hangar.jobs.duration` and `hangar.jobs.lease.expired`. | `jobs.Worker` |
| Jobs (02) | Schedules from 5-field cron in `server.timezone`; each run fires once across workers by compare-and-swap on `next_run_at`; a run joins the previous one if it is still active. | `DBQueue.SetSchedule`, `Worker.FireSchedules` |
| 11 | Leader election through `rate_limit_leases`, and `hangar.jobs.queued` computed by the leader every 60 seconds. `WorkerOptions.LeaderTasks` takes more gauges (`hangar.repos`, `hangar.users`). | `jobs.Leader`, `jobs.RecordQueueGauge` |
| PULL-7 | Shared bandwidth limiter: each busy process leases a slice of the budget in `rate_limit_leases` every 2 seconds; slices never add up to more than the budget; a stopped process's slice returns after 3 refreshes. Pull windows with overnight spans and daylight saving. | `jobs.DBLimiter`, `jobs.Windows` |
| OPS-4 | `gc` Job: unreferenced LFS objects after `gc.grace_period`, orphaned LFS blobs, retired, orphaned and dead pending packs, git data of purged Repos, stale `tmp/` and `exports/`, filesystem staging files older than 24 hours (`blob.StagingSweeper`), abandoned multipart uploads (filesystem); scopes `all`, `lfs`, `git`; reports `hangar.storage.bytes`. The orphan sweeps walk all of `lfs/` and `git/` on every run in batches of 500 and delete as they go, so memory stays bounded and no number of referenced objects stops a run before the last key. `upload.expire` Job for expired uploads. Registration with their schedules. | `internal/gc` |

| OPS-4, OPS-9 API | `GET /admin/storage`, `PUT /admin/quotas/{ns}` (audit event `quota.changed`), `POST /admin/gc`. | `internal/api/admin_storage.go` |

| decisions.md | `GET /admin/system` with doctor checks: configuration (when given), database, schema, Job backlog, clock skew against the database (Postgres) and the Blob store, Blob store round trip, presigned downloads (fetched from the server, URL never reported) and git 2.39 or later. `api.RunChecks` for a CLI `doctor`. | `internal/api/admin_system.go` |

## Security fixes

Three findings from review, each fixed with tests that fail without the fix.

| Finding | Fix | Tests |
|---|---|---|
| Stored XSS through the Blob store: presigned GETs set no `response-content-type` and no disposition without a filename, and writes did not pin `Content-Type`, so an object uploaded as `text/html` or `image/svg+xml` was served inline from the bucket's origin. | `blob.SafeContentType` (`application/octet-stream`). `PresignGet` always forces `response-content-type` and an attachment `response-content-disposition` (bare `attachment` without a filename). S3 pins `Content-Type` on server-side Puts, multipart initiation and copies (metadata replaced, not copied from the source). `PresignPut` returns `Content-Type` in `Headers` and, with a checksum, signs it. New `blob.Downloads.Serve` streams objects (proxy mode and the filesystem backend) with `blob.SetDownloadHeaders`: `application/octet-stream`, attachment, `nosniff`, overriding the caller's values. `blobtest.Fake` models S3: it stores a presigned PUT's type and honours the response overrides. | Conformance `ServedDownloadsAreAttachments` (fs, MinIO, fake) and `PresignedDownloadsAreAttachments` (MinIO, fake: a `text/html` upload through a plain presigned PUT downloads as an attachment; a checksummed PUT with another type is refused; presigned parts cannot set it); `TestStoredContentTypeIsPinned` (MinIO: Put, PutVerified, multipart and a copy of a `text/html` object); `TestPresignPutLimit` (signed headers and forced response overrides); `TestContentDisposition`, `TestSetDownloadHeadersOverridesCallerValues`. |
| Job authorisation: `GET /jobs/{id}`, the listing, cancel and retry trusted only "creator or Instance admin", so a Token restricted to one Repo saw other Repos' Jobs, and a user removed from a private Repo still saw its Job results (a zip download URL). | `jobs.NewJob.Repo` (column `jobs.repo_id`, request 6). `api.Jobs` takes `Authz` and `Repos` and checks `read_files` on the Job's Repo to see it and `write` to cancel or retry it (`admin` while the Repo is deleted; purged Repos' Jobs only for unrestricted Instance admins), always within Token restrictions. Restricted Tokens see no Instance-wide Jobs. The listing skips hidden Jobs and pages on (at most 10 queue pages per request, then returns the cursor). | `TestJobsCheckRepoAccess` (25 cases: Repo-restricted and Namespace-restricted Tokens, a read-scope Token, a restricted admin Token, deleted and purged Repos, GET, retry and listing), `TestJobsFollowRevokedRepoAccess` (demoted to read: 403 on cancel and retry; removed: 404 and the zip URL gone from GET and the list; collaborator Role restores it), `TestJobsListPagesPastHiddenJobs`, `TestQueueKeepsTheJobsRepo` (both drivers), `TestFakeKeepsRepoAndRedactsErrors`. |
| Secrets in Job errors: the worker recorded raw handler errors on spans (`span.RecordError`), in the `job finished` log record and in the Job's error column, so a wrapped `*url.Error` leaked a presigned URL; a panic stored `debug.Stack()` in the error column, which `GET /jobs/{id}` returns. | `jobs.RedactError` strips the query string, fragment and user information of every URL in an error's text (keeping scheme, host and path, with `?redacted`); the worker uses it for the stored error, the log record and a hand-built `exception` span event. A panic becomes a fixed message ("The Job stopped because of an internal error in Hangar. The server log has the details.") and the worker logs the redacted panic value and the stack at error level. `jobstest.Fake` stores errors the same way. | `TestWorkerRedactsURLsInErrors` (retry and permanent failure, both drivers: stored error, log and span events), `TestWorkerKeepsPanicStacksOutOfJobs`, `TestRedactURLs`, `TestRedactError`, `TestWorkerRetriesWithBackoffAndFails` (updated panic expectation). |

## Known gaps

- **Presigned PUTs without a checksum cannot pin `Content-Type`.** `huggingface_hub` sends no headers on a `basic` upload, and a signed header it leaves out fails the upload (research note, finding 4), so `PresignPut` signs the type only with a checksum. An uploader can then store any type, which is safe because no download serves the stored type: presigned GETs force `application/octet-stream` and an attachment, and `Serve` sets its own headers. S3 cannot send `X-Content-Type-Options` on a presigned GET; the forced type and attachment cover it. Stores that ignore `response-content-type` (none known; untested beyond MinIO) would serve the stored type.
- **Repo-scoped Jobs need `NewJob.Repo` from their owners** (request 6). Until W2, W3, W6, W7 and W10 set it, their Jobs are treated as Instance-wide: visible to the creator and unrestricted Instance admins, hidden from restricted Tokens, and not re-checked against the Repo.
- **AWS S3 was tested by hand, not in CI.** The S3 suite passed twice against AWS S3 in `eu-west-2` on 2026-10-15 (fix round 1), after the fixes for a missing bucket on `Stat` and for part uploads over slow links; the research note records the results and AWS's answers to presigned checksum PUTs. CI runs MinIO only. The busy-link failures of 2026-10-14 did not recur, so the new retries were seen on AWS only for `SlowDown`; the fault-injection tests cover resets, stalls and missing responses.
- **S3 part uploads spool to the temporary directory.** A part body that cannot be rewound is copied to `TMPDIR` while it is sent, so a retry can replay it: up to one part (16 MiB for objects up to 156 GiB) per upload in progress. The Compose examples mount `/tmp` as tmpfs, so there it uses memory.
- **S3 abandoned multipart uploads** are not listed by GC, because MinIO lists multipart uploads only for an exact object name. They are aborted by `upload.expire` from their rows; uploads that lost their row rely on the bucket's lifecycle rule (`AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload`, AWS) or MinIO's stale upload expiry (24 hours by default). The deployment docs (W9) should say so.
- **Unknown-size S3 Puts** buffer one part in memory (16 MiB at first, 128 MiB after 6,000 parts). Every LFS path knows its size and streams with no buffer; only zip exports and similar use unknown sizes.
- **`hangar.pull.rate_limited.duration`** is not recorded by the limiter, because `jobs.Limiter.WaitN` does not know the Upstream. W6 should time its `WaitN` calls and record it.
- **Unreachable git object pruning** inside packs is W2's `git.compact` (04 "Compaction"). GC deletes whole packs and orphaned pack files only.
- **The filesystem backend on NFS** is written for it (rename only, no locks) but was tested on the local disk only. `TestConcurrentPutAndDeleteInOneDirectory` found that a Delete pruning an empty directory could fail a concurrent Put into it on macOS (EINVAL and EEXIST, not only ENOENT); `install` now retries ENOENT and EINVAL, and EEXIST from `MkdirAll` only. EEXIST from `os.Rename` means the key's path is a directory, so it fails at once. NFS clients may report the race with other errors.
- **The clock check** compares this host with Postgres and with the Blob store's modification times; on SQLite with a local disk it has nothing to compare with. It cannot see skew between two Hangar hosts directly, only each host's skew against the shared database and store, which is what leases and grace periods depend on.

## What the integration lead must wire

In `cmd/hangar` (phase 0 wires fakes):

1. **Blob store:** `s, err := backends.Open(ctx, cfg.Storage)`, then `blob.Instrument(s, cfg.Storage.Backend, tel.Tracer(), inst.BlobOperationDuration)`, then the existing `ensureSentinel`. Give `backends.Downloads(cfg.Storage, store)` to W3 (LFS batch), W4 (`resolve`) and W8's browser downloads. When `RedirectURL` returns false they must stream with `Downloads.Serve(w, r, key, filename)` (or, if they stream another way, call `blob.SetDownloadHeaders` first), never set a `Content-Type` guessed from the file name.
2. **Queue and worker:** `loc, _ := time.LoadLocation(cfg.Server.Timezone)`; one `jobs.NewRegistry()`; `jobs.NewQueue(db, reg, jobs.QueueOptions{Location: loc})` for every process. For roles `all` and `worker`, `jobs.NewWorker(db, reg, jobs.WorkerOptions{Concurrency: cfg.Jobs.Workers, Lease: cfg.Jobs.Lease, Location: loc, InstanceLimits: map[jobs.Kind]int{jobs.KindPullFile: cfg.Pull.Concurrency}, LeaderTasks: []func(context.Context) error{jobs.RecordQueueGauge(db, inst)}, Logger: log, Tracer: tel.Tracer(), Instrument: inst})` and `go worker.Run(ctx)`. Register every handler before `Run`. On shutdown, `Run` returns Jobs to the queue.
3. **GC:** `c := gc.New(db, store, gc.Options{GracePeriod: cfg.GC.GracePeriod, PackGracePeriod: cfg.Git.PackGracePeriod, PendingPackAge: cfg.Git.Timeout + cfg.Git.PackGracePeriod, Logger: log, Instrument: inst})`, then `gc.Register(ctx, reg, queue, c, cfg.GC.Schedule)` once at start-up on a worker-capable process. `hangar admin gc [--git]` is `gc.Start(ctx, queue, gc.ScopeAll or gc.ScopeGit, uuid.Nil)`.
4. **Limiter and windows for W6:** `jobs.NewLimiter(db, jobs.LimiterOptions{Owner: worker.Owner(), Budget: <reads pull.bandwidth_limit, or the Instance setting if W5 adds one>})`, used with the name `"pull"`; call `Close` on shutdown. `jobs.ParseWindows(cfg.Pull.Windows, loc)`; a `pull.file` handler outside a window returns `jobs.Snooze(w.NextOpen(now), w.WaitMessage())` unless the Pull has the **Pull now** override.
5. **Quotas for W2, W3, W6 and W11:** `gc.NewAccounting(db)`. Before storing, compute `adding` (pack size plus `NewLFSBytes` of the new objects) and call `CheckQuota`; map `gc.ErrQuotaExceeded` to the protocol's error (Hub 403 with the message, git `PreReceive` rejection, native 403).
6. **Native API:** compose `&api.Jobs{Queue: queue, Authz: authz, Repos: repoService}` (both required: without them Repo-scoped Jobs are hidden and the request fails), `&api.AdminStorage{Authz: authz, Accounting: accounting, Queue: queue, Audit: recorder}` and `&api.AdminSystem{Authz: authz, DB: db, Info: api.SystemInfo{Version: version, Commit: commit, Role: cfg.Server.Role, BlobBackend: cfg.Storage.Backend, DownloadMode: <cfg.Storage.S3.DownloadMode on S3, else empty>, Telemetry: tel.Exporters}, Checks: api.DoctorChecks(db, api.DoctorOptions{Store: store, Downloads: downloads, Config: cfg})}`; `hangar admin doctor` (W9) runs the same checks with `api.RunChecks` into the server (see request 4).
7. **`make test`** now sets `HANGAR_TEST_MINIO=1` (request 1), and so does CI's `go-test` job (request 5); both need Docker for MinIO.
